faq.question: What kind of boat is this?
faq.answer: A 44-foot, full-displacement trawler yacht with a welded steel hull, built for long-range coastal and inland cruising rather than planing performance.

faq.question: How fast does it cruise, and how far can it go?
faq.answer: Cruising speed is 8 knots at a quiet 1,800 rpm, with range approaching 1,000 nautical miles - roughly 125 running hours at cruise speed, about 1,850 km.

faq.question: What engine is fitted?
faq.answer: A 250 hp Cummins 6.7-litre marine diesel: heavy duty, warranted for continuous duty, fully certified to US EPA Tier 3, with Cummins service widely available in North America.

faq.question: Can it do the Great Loop?
faq.answer: She is designed to be Great Loop compatible: low-profile flybridge and folding radar arch keep air draft in check, and 44 ft LOA suits smaller marinas and locks. Confirm exact clearances against the current specification.

faq.question: Is it an ocean-capable boat?
faq.answer: The design target is ISO/CE Category A, the ocean category for extended voyages. Category A is a design and certification standard; ask for the current compliance status of the boat in build.

faq.question: How is the steel protected against rust?
faq.answer: Certified welding, abrasive blasting to white metal, an AwlGrip rust-inhibiting epoxy coating system, and an AwlCraft urethane topcoat.

faq.question: Can I see the drawings, and what does it cost?
faq.answer: The current specification, general arrangement drawings and coating schedule are available to prospective owners. Pricing, delivery and specification options are discussed directly; enquire via https://gentectld.com/.
